To talk about your own husband politely, say 제 남편 or 저희 남편. For someone else's husband, say 남편분 rather than plain 남편.
남편 is pronounced nam-pyeon, with the ㅍ breathy like the p in "pen."

faq.q: What do Korean wives call their husbands?
faq.a: Most often 여보 (yeobo) or 자기야 (jagiya). Younger wives often say 오빠 (oppa) too.

faq.q: Is 신랑 the same as husband?
faq.a: 신랑 means groom, but in casual talk many women use it to mean their husband, as in 우리 신랑 (my hubby).

intro: "Wife" in Korean is 아내 (anae). In everyday speech many Korean men also say 와이프 (waipeu), from the English word, and couples call each other 여보 (yeobo), "honey."

ways.note: The standard word for wife. Correct in both speech and writing.
From English "wife." Very common in casual conversation: 우리 와이프 (my wife).
What married couples call each other, like "honey." Used to address your spouse, not to talk about her.
A polite word for someone else's wife. Avoid using it for your own wife.
A very respectful word for the wife of a boss, teacher or someone senior.
Literally "house person." An older, humble way some men refer to their own wife. Sounds old-fashioned to many young people.

examples.context: Introducing your wife
Chatting with a friend
examples.en: I watched a movie with my wife.

examples.context: Asking politely about someone's wife

tips: Use 아내 or 와이프 for your own wife, and 부인 or 사모님 for someone else's wife. Calling your own wife 부인 sounds strange, and calling a boss's wife 아내 sounds too plain.
When talking to your wife, use 여보 or 자기야, not 아내. Just like English speakers do not usually say "Wife, where are you?"
와이프 is so common in speech that many Korean men use it more than 아내. In writing and formal speech, 아내 is the safer choice.

faq.q: What do Korean husbands call their wives?
faq.a: To her face, usually 여보 (yeobo) or 자기야 (jagiya). When talking about her, 아내 or 와이프.

faq.q: What is the difference between 아내 and 부인?
faq.a: 아내 is for your own wife. 부인 is a polite word for another person's wife.

intro: "Boy" in Korean is 소년 (sonyeon), the word you see in titles, stories and the name 방탄소년단 (BTS). In everyday conversation, Koreans usually say 남자아이 (namja-ai) or the casual 남자애 (namja-ae) for a boy.

ways.note: "Boy" or "young lad." Common in writing, songs, titles and group names. Sounds a little literary in daily talk.
"Male child." The natural everyday word for a little boy.
A shortened, casual form of 남자아이. Also used by teens for boys their own age.
A male student, often used for school-age boys.
"Kiddo" or "little one." For a small child of any gender.

examples.context: Asking about a child
Telling a story
At the park

tips: 소년 is a lovely word for names, captions and tattoos, and it is the 소년 in 방탄소년단 (BTS, "Bulletproof Boy Scouts"). In a normal conversation, though, 남자아이 or 남자애 sounds more natural.
Teenagers and young adults often just say 남자 (namja, "guy" or "man") for boys their age, as in 그 남자 누구야? (Who is that guy?).
For your own son, use 아들 (adeul) instead of 소년 or 남자아이.

faq.q: What does 소년 mean in BTS?
faq.a: BTS is 방탄소년단 (bangtan sonyeondan) in Korean, and 소년 means boy. The name means "Bulletproof Boy Scouts."

faq.q: How do you say "boyfriend" in Korean?
faq.a: Boyfriend is 남자친구 (namjachingu), often shortened to 남친 (namchin).

intro: "Girl" in Korean is 소녀 (sonyeo), the word used in titles, songs and the group name 소녀시대 (Girls' Generation). In everyday speech, Koreans usually say 여자아이 (yeoja-ai) or the casual 여자애 (yeoja-ae).

ways.note: "Girl" or "young maiden." Common in writing, songs and titles. Sounds a little literary in daily talk.
"Female child." The natural everyday word for a little girl.
A shortened, casual form of 여자아이. Teens also use it for girls their own age.
A female student, often used for school-age girls.
A young, unmarried woman, like "miss" or "young lady." Can sound old-fashioned or awkward when calling out to a stranger.

examples.context: Seeing a child
Telling a story
Describing a scene

tips: 소녀 is a pretty word for captions, names and tattoos, and it appears in many K-pop names like 소녀시대 (Girls' Generation). In normal conversation, 여자아이 or 여자애 sounds more natural.
For girls or women their own age, young people usually say 여자 (yeoja, "girl" or "woman"), as in 그 여자 누구야? (Who is that girl?).
For your own daughter, use 딸 (ttal) instead of 소녀.

faq.q: What is the difference between 소녀 and 여자?
faq.a: 소녀 means a young girl and sounds a bit literary. 여자 means female, woman or girl, and is the everyday word for a girl or woman of any age.

faq.q: How do you say "girlfriend" in Korean?
faq.a: Girlfriend is 여자친구 (yeojachingu), often shortened to 여친 (yeochin).

intro: "Person" in Korean is 사람 (saram). It is one of the most useful words in Korean, used for people in general and for nationality, like 한국 사람 (Korean person). For politeness, Koreans replace it with 분 (bun).

ways.note: The everyday word for person or people.
The honorific word for a person. Used instead of 사람 to show respect: 이분 (this person), 어떤 분 (someone).
"People." 들 makes it plural, though Koreans often leave it out when the meaning is clear.
"Human being." Used for humans as a species. Said about someone in casual talk, it can sound harsh.
The counter for people: 세 명 (three people). Polite version: 분, as in 세 분.

examples.context: Describing a friend
Asking politely who someone is
At a busy place
examples.en: There are a lot of people.

tips: Add a country name before 사람 to say someone's nationality: 한국 사람 (Korean), 미국 사람 (American), 영국 사람 (British).
When talking about someone older or a customer, use 분 instead of 사람. Restaurant staff ask 몇 분이세요? (How many people?) rather than using 사람.
사람 is also used in sayings and song lyrics about love, like 내 사람 (my person, the one I love).

faq.q: How do you say "people" in Korean?
faq.a: 사람들 (saramdeul). Often just 사람 is enough, for example 사람이 많아요 means "there are a lot of people."

faq.q: How do you say "Korean person"?
faq.a: 한국 사람 (hanguk saram). The more formal word is 한국인 (hangugin).

intro: "Cousin" in Korean is 사촌 (sachon). Koreans usually add a sibling word after it to show the cousin's age and gender, like 사촌 동생 (younger cousin) or 사촌 언니 (older female cousin, said by a girl).

ways.note: The general word for cousin. Literally "four chon," counting the family distance between you.
A cousin on your mother's side. 외 marks the mother's side.
A younger cousin, any gender.
An older female cousin, said by a girl or woman. A boy would say 사촌 누나 (sachon nuna).
An older male cousin, said by a boy or man. A girl would say 사촌 오빠 (sachon oppa).
"Relative." Use it for relatives in general, or for cousins further away than 사촌.

examples.context: Talking about family abroad
Telling a friend about your weekend
examples.en: I hung out with my younger cousin.

examples.context: Sharing family news
examples.en: My older cousin is getting married.

tips: Koreans count family distance in 촌 (chon). Your parent is one chon away, a sibling two, an uncle three (삼촌), and a cousin four (사촌). That is where the word comes from.
Inside the family, cousins rarely call each other 사촌. They use sibling words directly: 언니, 오빠, 누나, 형 or the cousin's name.

faq.q: How do you say "my cousin" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 제 사촌 (je sachon) politely or 내 사촌 (nae sachon) casually. More often people add age and gender, like 사촌 동생 or 사촌 언니.

faq.q: Do Koreans call cousins by sibling names?
faq.a: Yes. Cousins usually call each other 언니, 오빠, 누나, 형 or 동생, just like siblings.

intro: "Korea" in Korean is 한국 (hanguk). The official name of South Korea is 대한민국 (daehanminguk), and South Koreans often just say 우리나라 (urinara), "our country."

ways.note: The everyday word for Korea. In South Korea it means South Korea.
The official name, "Republic of Korea." Heard in sports cheers, news and anthems.
"Our country." How South Koreans usually refer to Korea among themselves.
"South Korea," used when contrasting with the North.
"North Korea," as said in South Korea.
The English word "Korea" written in Hangeul. Seen in brand names, slogans and events.

examples.context: Sharing a travel dream
examples.en: I want to go to Korea.

examples.context: Cheering at a match
Talking about what you like

tips: 한국 doubles as the adjective "Korean": 한국 음식 (Korean food), 한국 사람 (Korean person), 한국 드라마 (Korean drama). The language is 한국어.
At sports games, fans chant 대한민국 with five claps. It is one of the most recognizable cheers in Korea.
In North Korea, the country is called 조선 (joseon), not 한국. When South Koreans say 한국, they mean South Korea.

faq.q: How do you say "South Korea" in Korean?
faq.a: In South Korea people just say 한국. The official name is 대한민국, and 남한 is used when contrasting with North Korea.

faq.q: How do you say "I love Korea" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 한국을 사랑해요 (hangugeul saranghaeyo), or more casually 한국 너무 좋아요 (hanguk neomu joayo), "I really like Korea."

intro: "Korean" (the language) in Korean is 한국어 (hangugeo). In everyday speech Koreans often say 한국말 (hangungmal), and the Korean alphabet itself is called 한글 (hangeul).

ways.note: The standard name of the language. Used in textbooks, classes and apps.
"Korean speech." More conversational, very common when talking about speaking Korean.
The Korean alphabet, not the language. You read and write 한글; you speak 한국어.
"National language." Koreans use it for Korean as a school subject.

examples.context: Telling someone what you study
A compliment you might hear
Encouraging a new learner

tips: Many learners mix up 한글 and 한국어. 한글 is the writing system created in the 1400s; 한국어 is the language itself.
한국말 is pronounced hangungmal, not hanguk-mal, because the ㄱ before ㅁ softens into an "ng" sound.
If Koreans say 한국말 잘하시네요 (you speak Korean well), a humble reply is 아니에요, 아직 많이 부족해요 (No, I still have a long way to go).

faq.q: Is it 한국어 or 한국말?
faq.a: Both are correct. 한국어 is a little more formal and used in classes; 한국말 is more common in casual conversation.

faq.q: How do you say "I speak Korean"?
faq.a: Say 한국어 할 줄 알아요 (hangugeo hal jul arayo), "I can speak Korean," or 한국어 조금 해요 (hangugeo jogeum haeyo), "I speak a little Korean."

intro: "English" (the language) in Korean is 영어 (yeongeo). If you mean an English person, the word is 영국 사람 (yeongguk saram), since 영국 means England or the UK.

ways.note: The English language.
"In English." 로 means "in" or "by means of."
An English or British person. 영국 is the UK or England.
English text or writing, as in 영문 이름 (your name written in English letters).

examples.context: Asking if someone speaks English
Asking for a translation
Introducing your job

tips: Korean names languages by adding 어 (eo, language) to the country: 영어 (English), 한국어 (Korean), 일본어 (Japanese), 중국어 (Chinese). Note that it is 영어, not 영국어.
Pronounce 영어 as yeong-eo, two syllables. The "ng" carries smoothly into the second vowel.
Many Koreans study English for years in school, but some feel shy about speaking it. Trying a little Korean first is a kind way to start.

faq.q: How do you ask "Do you speak English?" in Korean?
faq.a: Ask 영어 할 줄 아세요? (yeongeo hal jul aseyo) to be extra polite, or 영어 할 줄 알아요? in standard polite speech.

faq.q: How do you say "I speak English" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 저는 영어를 해요 (jeoneun yeongeoreul haeyo), or 영어 할 줄 알아요 (I can speak English).

intro: "Food" in Korean is 음식 (eumsik). In daily life Koreans also say 밥 (bap), which means rice and also "a meal," and 먹을 거 (meogeul geo), "something to eat."

ways.note: The general word for food or a dish: 한국 음식 (Korean food), 매운 음식 (spicy food).
Cooked rice, and by extension any meal. 밥 먹었어? means "Have you eaten?"
"Something to eat." Natural in casual speech: 먹을 거 있어? (Is there anything to eat?)
Cooking, or a prepared dish. 요리하다 means "to cook."
"A meal," more formal than 밥. Common in polite phrases like 식사하셨어요? (Have you had your meal?)

examples.context: After a meal out
Getting to know someone
Checking on a friend

tips: 밥 is so central that Koreans use "Did you eat?" (밥 먹었어?) as a caring greeting, a bit like "How are you?"
음식 is pronounced eum-sik. The first syllable has a vowel that does not exist in English; say "uh" with your lips spread flat, not rounded.
Delivery food is 배달 음식 (baedal eumsik) and late-night snacks are 야식 (yasik), two words you will see often in K-dramas.

faq.q: How do you say "Korean food" in Korean?
faq.a: 한국 음식 (hanguk eumsik). You may also see 한식 (hansik), a shorter word for Korean cuisine.

faq.q: How do you say "I love Korean food"?
faq.a: Say 한국 음식 정말 좋아해요 (hanguk eumsik jeongmal joahaeyo), "I really like Korean food."

intro: "Rice" in Korean is 밥 (bap) when it is cooked and ready to eat, and 쌀 (ssal) when it is the raw grain you buy in a bag. 밥 also means "a meal" in general, which shows how central rice is to Korean life.

ways.note: Cooked rice, and also "meal." The word you will use most.
Uncooked rice, the grain. 쌀 사러 가요 means "I'm going to buy rice."
A bowl of steamed rice, as ordered at a restaurant.
Plain white rice, as opposed to rice mixed with other grains (잡곡밥).
The honorific word for an elder's meal. 할머니, 진지 드세요 means "Grandma, please eat."
The rice plant growing in the field.

examples.context: Calling everyone to the table
Ordering at a restaurant
Writing a shopping list

tips: Fried rice is 볶음밥 (bokkeumbap) and mixed rice is 비빔밥 (bibimbap). Many dish names end in 밥, so you will start recognizing it on menus.
밥 ends with a stopped "p" sound: close your lips but don't release a puff of air. 쌀 starts with a tense ㅆ, a sharper "ss."
With grandparents or elders, use 진지 instead of 밥: 진지 드셨어요? (Have you eaten?) sounds very respectful.

faq.q: What is the difference between 밥 and 쌀?
faq.a: 쌀 is raw, uncooked rice grain. Once it is cooked, it becomes 밥.

faq.q: Why does 밥 mean meal?
faq.a: Rice is the base of almost every Korean meal, so 밥 came to mean the meal itself. 밥 먹자 means "Let's eat," even if you eat noodles.

intro: "Coffee" in Korean is 커피 (keopi), borrowed from English. Korea has a huge café culture, and the most popular order by far is 아메리카노 (amerikano), especially iced.

ways.note: Coffee. Korean has no "f" sound, so it is said with a "p."
Americano, the default coffee order in Korea.
Slang for 아이스 아메리카노, iced americano. Very common among young people.
Café or coffee shop.
Instant coffee mix in a stick, with sugar and creamer. A classic in Korean offices and homes.

examples.context: Ordering at a café
Offering a coworker a drink
Inviting a friend out

tips: Koreans drink iced americano even in winter, which led to the joke word 얼죽아 (eoljuga), short for "I'd rather freeze to death than drink hot coffee."
Say 커피 as keo-pi, with the first vowel like the "u" in "cup." Saying "ko-fee" may not be understood right away.
To order, add 주세요 (please): 따뜻한 아메리카노 주세요 is "A hot americano, please," and 아이스 아메리카노 주세요 is the iced one.

faq.q: How do you order coffee in Korean?
faq.a: Say the drink plus 주세요: 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요 (amerikano han jan juseyo), "One americano, please."

faq.q: What does 아아 mean?
faq.a: 아아 is slang for 아이스 아메리카노, iced americano. Its hot counterpart is 뜨아 (tteua), short for 뜨거운 아메리카노.

intro: "Today" in Korean is 오늘 (oneul). It is a native Korean word you will hear constantly, from plans with friends to the weather forecast. It works in any situation, casual or polite.

ways.note: The everyday word for today. Use it with anyone.
Tonight. 오늘 저녁 (oneul jeonyeok) means this evening.
This morning.
Nowadays, these days. Used for talking about the present era, not this particular day.
A formal Sino-Korean word for today, seen on notices and official signs, such as a shop sign saying it is closed today. People do not say it in conversation.

examples.context: Asking a friend about their plans
Commenting on a sunny day
Telling a coworker you are off

tips: 오늘 is pronounced roughly "oh-nool", with a light ㄹ at the end. The "eu" in the romanization is a short sound made with the lips relaxed, not rounded.
On social media you will often see 오늘도 (oneuldo), "today too", in captions like 오늘도 화이팅 ("fighting again today"). It is a warm, everyday way to cheer yourself or others on.
Watch out for 금일 on signs. Some Koreans mistake it for 금요일 (Friday) because both start with 금, but 금일 just means today.

faq.q: How do you say "tonight" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 오늘 밤 (oneul bam) for tonight, or 오늘 저녁 (oneul jeonyeok) for this evening.

faq.q: How do you say "today is..." in Korean?
faq.a: Use 오늘은 ... 이에요/예요. For example, 오늘은 월요일이에요 (oneureun woryoirieyo) means "Today is Monday."

intro: "Tomorrow" in Korean is 내일 (naeil). You can use it with anyone, and it often comes up in goodbyes like 내일 봐 (naeil bwa), "see you tomorrow".

ways.note: The everyday word for tomorrow. Use it in any situation.
"See you tomorrow" to a friend or someone younger.
"See you tomorrow" to a coworker, teacher or anyone you speak to politely.
The day after tomorrow.
Also the day after tomorrow. It is also used loosely to mean "very soon".
A formal written word for tomorrow, seen in old notices or official documents. Not used in speech.

examples.context: Saying goodbye to a classmate
Asking a friend to hang out
Checking the weather forecast

tips: Korean often uses the present tense for planned or expected future events, so 내일 비가 와요 (literally "tomorrow it rains") is a completely natural way to say it will rain tomorrow.
Pronounce 내일 as two clear syllables, "nae-il", close to "neh-eel". The ㄹ at the end is light.
Unlike 오늘 (today) and 어제 (yesterday), which are native Korean words, 내일 comes from Chinese characters.

faq.q: How do you say "see you tomorrow" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 내일 봐 (naeil bwa) to friends, and 내일 봬요 (naeil bwaeyo) when you need to be polite.

faq.q: How do you say "the day after tomorrow" in Korean?
faq.a: It is 모레 (more). 내일모레 (naeilmore) means the same thing and is also common.

intro: "Yesterday" in Korean is 어제 (eoje). It is a native Korean word that works with anyone, casual or polite. A slightly longer form, 어저께 (eojeokke), means exactly the same thing.

ways.note: The everyday word for yesterday.
Same meaning as 어제. It sounds a little more chatty and conversational.
Last night.
The day before yesterday. The short form 그제 (geuje) is also common.

examples.context: Catching up with a friend
Explaining why you look worn out
Noticing the wet streets in the morning

tips: 어제 is pronounced roughly "uh-jeh". The first vowel is the open "uh" sound, not "oh".
When you talk about yesterday, the verb goes into the past tense, usually with 았/었. For example, 먹어요 (I eat) becomes 먹었어요 (I ate).
In everyday speech 어제 is by far the most common choice. 어저께 is not slang, so it is fine to use, but you will hear it less.

faq.q: Is there a difference between 어제 and 어저께?
faq.a: No, they mean the same thing. 어제 is shorter and more common, while 어저께 sounds a little more conversational.

faq.q: How do you say "last night" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 어젯밤 (eojetbam). For yesterday evening, say 어제 저녁 (eoje jeonyeok).

intro: "Morning" in Korean is 아침 (achim). The same word also means breakfast, so 아침 먹었어? means "Did you eat breakfast?" For clock times, Koreans use 오전 (ojeon) for a.m.

ways.note: Morning, and also breakfast. The everyday word.
Before noon, a.m. Used with times: 오전 9시 (ojeon ahop si) is 9 a.m.
"Good morning." A friendly, light greeting, popular in texts and among friends.
Breakfast, said clearly as a meal (밥 means rice or meal).
Dawn, or the very early hours after midnight. 새벽 2시 is 2 a.m.

examples.context: Texting a friend when you wake up
A parent checking on their child
Making plans with a coworker

tips: 좋은 아침 sounds a bit like a translation of the English greeting. It is friendly and common in texts, but in person many Koreans simply say 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo), or ask 잘 잤어? (jal jasseo?), "Did you sleep well?"
Because 아침 means both morning and breakfast, context tells you which one is meant. 아침 먹었어? is almost always about breakfast.
아침 is pronounced "ah-chim". The ㅊ is a breathy "ch" sound.

faq.q: How do you say "good morning" in Korean?
faq.a: Casually, 좋은 아침 (joeun achim). Politely, most people just say 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo), which works at any time of day.

faq.q: How do you say "a.m." in Korean?
faq.a: Use 오전 (ojeon) before the time, for example 오전 10시 (ojeon yeol si), 10 a.m. For p.m. use 오후 (ohu).

intro: "Night" in Korean is 밤 (bam). Koreans also use 저녁 (jeonyeok) for the evening, roughly from sunset until bedtime. For "good night", friends say 잘 자 (jal ja).

ways.note: Night, the dark hours. The basic everyday word.
Evening. It also means dinner, like 아침 means both morning and breakfast.
Tonight.
A Sino-Korean word for night-time, used in compounds and on signs, such as 야간 근무 (night shift).
"Good night", literally "sleep well". To elders, say 안녕히 주무세요 (annyeonghi jumuseyo).

examples.context: Promising to call your partner
Telling a friend you have trouble sleeping
examples.en: I can't fall asleep at night.

examples.context: Asking a family member about dinner

tips: 밤 also means chestnut. The spelling is the same, so context tells you which one is meant. As a tattoo or caption on its own, people may read it either way, so a phrase like 밤하늘 (bamhaneul, night sky) or 별밤 (byeolbam, starry night) is clearer and more poetic.
Koreans draw the line between 저녁 and 밤 differently from English. 7 p.m. is usually 저녁, and 밤 starts later, roughly after 9 or 10 p.m.
A late-night snack has its own word: 야식 (yasik). Fried chicken is a classic 야식.

faq.q: How do you say "good night" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 잘 자 (jal ja) to friends and family your age or younger, 잘 자요 (jal jayo) politely, and 안녕히 주무세요 (annyeonghi jumuseyo) to elders.

faq.q: What is the difference between 밤 and 저녁?
faq.a: 저녁 is the evening and also means dinner. 밤 is the later, dark part of the night.

intro: "Home" in Korean is 집 (jip). The same word means house, apartment or any place you live. Koreans usually say 우리 집 (uri jip), "our home", even when talking about their own home.

ways.note: Home, house. The everyday word for where you live.
"My home", literally "our home". This is what Koreans naturally say instead of 내 집.
An honorific word for someone else's home, used for elders or customers: 댁이 어디세요? (Where do you live?).
Hometown, the place you come from.
Home in the sense of household or family life, as in 가정 요리 (home cooking).

examples.context: Feeling worn out at the end of the day
Answering a friend who asks where you are
Inviting a friend over

tips: Koreans say 우리 집 ("our home") rather than 내 집 ("my home"), because a home is thought of as shared with your family. 내 집 sounds like you are talking about owning property.
When a vowel follows, the final ㅂ of 집 links to it: 집에 is pronounced "ji-beh" (jibe). On its own, 집 ends with the lips closed, without a puff of air.
When you come home, Koreans say 다녀왔습니다 (danyeowatseumnida) or casually 다녀왔어 (danyeowasseo), "I'm back". The family answers 왔어? or 다녀왔어?

faq.q: How do you say "I'm home" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 다녀왔습니다 (danyeowatseumnida) politely, or 다녀왔어 (danyeowasseo) casually. It literally means "I went and came back".

faq.q: How do you say "go home" in Korean?
faq.a: "Go home" is 집에 가다 (jibe gada). "I'm going home" is 집에 가요 (jibe gayo).

intro: "School" in Korean is 학교 (hakgyo). It is the general word for any school, and it also forms the names of each level, like 고등학교 (godeunghakgyo, high school). It works in any situation.

ways.note: School in general. The everyday word.
Elementary school (grades 1 to 6).
Middle school (grades 7 to 9).
High school (grades 10 to 12). A high school student is a 고등학생 (godeunghaksaeng).
University or college. Also shortened to 대학 (daehak).
A private after-school academy or cram school, a huge part of student life in Korea.

examples.context: Rushing out the door in the morning
examples.en: I have to go to school.

examples.context: Asking a younger sibling in the afternoon
Meeting a new student
examples.en: Which school do you go to?

tips: 학교 is pronounced "hak-kyo". The ㄱ in 교 sounds tense, like a sharp "k", because it follows the ㄱ of 학.
To say you attend a school, use 다니다 (to attend, go regularly): 학교에 다녀요 (I go to school). 가다 (to go) is for the trip itself, like heading to school this morning.
School dramas are full of words like 선배 (sunbae, an older student), 후배 (hoobae, a younger student) and 반 (ban, homeroom class).

faq.q: How do you say "student" in Korean?
faq.a: A student is 학생 (haksaeng). A university student is 대학생 (daehaksaeng).

faq.q: What is a hagwon?
faq.a: 학원 (hagwon) is a private academy where students take extra classes after school, often for English, math or exam prep.

intro: "Money" in Korean is 돈 (don). It is the everyday word for money in any form and works in any situation. Korean currency is the 원 (won).

ways.note: Money in general. The everyday word.
Cash.
A bank or credit card, the most common way to pay in Korea.
The Korean currency, written ₩. 천 원 (cheon won) is 1,000 won.
Pocket money or an allowance, often given by parents or grandparents.
A monthly salary. 월급날 (wolgeumnal) is payday.

examples.context: Explaining why you can't go out
Asking a friend for a small loan
examples.en: Can you lend me some money?

examples.context: Telling a friend after a family visit

tips: Prices in Korea use the Sino-Korean numbers: 오천 원 (ocheon won) is 5,000 won. To ask a price, say 얼마예요? (eolmayeyo?), "How much is it?"
At Lunar New Year, children bow to their elders and receive 세뱃돈 (sebaetdon), New Year's money, usually in an envelope.
Cards are accepted almost everywhere in Korea, even for small amounts, so 카드 돼요? is a question you rarely need. Some street food stalls and markets still prefer cash.

faq.q: What is Korean money called?
faq.a: The Korean currency is the won, 원 (won), written with the symbol ₩.

faq.q: How do you say "I have no money" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 돈이 없어요 (doni eopseoyo) politely, or 돈 없어 (don eopseo) casually with friends.

intro: "Weekend" in Korean is 주말 (jumal). It literally means "the end of the week" and works in any situation. To wish someone a good weekend, say 주말 잘 보내세요 (jumal jal bonaeseyo).

ways.note: Weekend. The everyday word.
This weekend. Next weekend is 다음 주말 (daeum jumal).
"Have a good weekend." A common goodbye on Friday at work or school.
"Have a good weekend" to a friend.
Weekday, Monday to Friday.
Slang for Friday night, short for 불타는 금요일, "burning Friday", the start of the weekend fun.

examples.context: Asking a friend about weekend plans
examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?

examples.context: Leaving the office on Friday
Turning down an invitation

tips: 주말 is pronounced "joo-mal". The ㅈ is softer than an English "j", and the ㄹ at the end is light.
On Monday you might hear people complain about 월요병 (woryobyeong), literally "Monday sickness", the Korean version of the Monday blues.
For "have a good weekend", 주말 잘 보내세요 is the safe choice with coworkers, teachers and people you don't know well.

faq.q: How do you say "have a good weekend" in Korean?
faq.a: Say 주말 잘 보내세요 (jumal jal bonaeseyo) politely, or 주말 잘 보내 (jumal jal bonae) to a friend.

faq.q: How do you say "weekday" in Korean?
faq.a: A weekday is 평일 (pyeongil). Koreans often contrast 평일 and 주말, for example when talking about opening hours.

intro: Numbers 1 to 10 in Korean start with 하나, 둘, 셋 (hana, dul, set), "one, two, three". Korean actually has two sets of numbers: native Korean numbers (하나 to 열) and Sino-Korean numbers (일 to 십). Which one you use depends on what you are counting.

ways.ko: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 다섯, 여섯, 일곱, 여덟, 아홉, 열
ways.roman: hana, dul, set, net, daseot, yeoseot, ilgop, yeodeol, ahop, yeol
ways.note: Native Korean numbers 1 to 10. Used for counting things and people, for age (열 살, ten years old) and for the hour when telling time (세 시, three o'clock).

ways.ko: 일, 이, 삼, 사, 오, 육, 칠, 팔, 구, 십
ways.roman: il, i, sam, sa, o, yuk, chil, pal, gu, sip
ways.note: Sino-Korean numbers 1 to 10. Used for money, dates, phone numbers, floors, minutes and math. For example, 삼십 분 is 30 minutes.
The short forms of 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, used right before a counter word: 한 개 (one item), 두 명 (two people), 세 시 (three o'clock).
Zero. In phone numbers people usually say 공 (gong) instead, so 010 is read 공일공 (gong-il-gong).

examples.context: Counting down before taking a photo
Buying fruit at a market
Giving directions in a building

tips: A simple rule of thumb: count things, people, age and hours with native numbers (하나, 둘, 셋), and use Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼) for money, dates, minutes, floors and phone numbers. So 3:30 is 세 시 삼십 분 (se si samsip bun), mixing both.
Some spellings don't match the sound. 여덟 (eight) is pronounced "yeo-deol", and 넷 and 셋 end in a clipped "t" sound. 육 (six) becomes "ryuk" or "nyuk" in some combinations, like 십육 (sim-nyuk, sixteen).
Koreans often count down with 하나, 둘, 셋! before a photo or a group action.

faq.q: Why does Korean have two number systems?
faq.a: Korean has its own native numbers and a second set borrowed from Chinese. Both are used every day, each for different things, so learners need both.

faq.q: Which numbers do you use for age in Korean?
faq.a: In everyday speech, native numbers with 살: 스무 살 (seumu sal) is 20 years old. In formal writing, Sino-Korean numbers with 세 are used, such as 20세.

faq.q: How do you count to 10 in Korean?
faq.a: Native Korean: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 다섯, 여섯, 일곱, 여덟, 아홉, 열. Sino-Korean: 일, 이, 삼, 사, 오, 육, 칠, 팔, 구, 십.

intro: "Love" in Korean is 사랑 (sarang). It is the everyday word for love of every kind: romantic love, love for family, and love for friends or things. Add 해 and you get 사랑해 (saranghae), "I love you."

ways.note: The standard word for love. Works on its own as a noun, in captions, and in tattoos.
"I love you." The verb form, used between partners, close friends and family.
First love. A very common word in songs, dramas and everyday talk.
Affection or fondness. A softer, more formal word than 사랑, often used in writing.
The English loanword "love." Seen in brand names, song titles and slang, but 사랑 is what people say.

examples.context: Talking with a friend about a breakup
Hearing an old song on the radio
examples.en: It reminds me of my first love.

examples.context: Hanging up a phone call with your mom

tips: 사랑 looks and sounds good on its own, so it is a popular choice for tattoos, necklaces and captions. The r in sarang is a light tap, closer to a soft d than an English r.
Koreans say 사랑해 less often than English speakers say "I love you," especially to parents. Many people show love with actions or with phrases like 보고 싶어 (I miss you) instead.
내 사랑 (nae sarang) means "my love" and is used as a pet name, often a bit playfully.

faq.q: How do you write love in Korean?
faq.a: Love is written 사랑 in Hangul and pronounced sa-rang.

faq.q: What is the difference between sarang and saranghae?
faq.a: 사랑 (sarang) is the noun "love." 사랑해 (saranghae) is the verb form and means "I love you."

faq.q: Is 사랑 a good tattoo word?
faq.a: Yes. 사랑 is a complete, natural word on its own and simply means love.

intro: "Heart" in Korean is 마음 (maeum) when you mean feelings, as in a kind heart or a broken heart. The heart that beats in your chest is 심장 (simjang), and the heart shape or emoji is 하트 (hateu).

ways.note: Heart as in feelings, mind and spirit. The word to use for emotions.
The physical heart, the organ. Also used for a pounding heart from excitement.
The heart shape, from English "heart." Used for emojis, drawings and finger hearts.
Literally "chest," but often used for feelings felt in the chest, like heartache.
A short, spoken form of 마음. Common in casual speech and texts.

examples.context: Hearing sad news
Right before going on stage
Texting a friend

tips: English "heart" covers three Korean words. Use 마음 for feelings, 심장 for the organ, and 하트 for the shape. Using 심장 for feelings can sound medical or very dramatic.
The K-pop finger heart, made by crossing your thumb and index finger, is called 손하트 (sonhateu), "hand heart."
For a tattoo or caption, 마음 is the warm, poetic choice. It also appears in phrases like 내 마음 (nae maeum), "my heart."

faq.q: What is the Korean word for heart?
faq.a: For feelings, it is 마음 (maeum). For the organ it is 심장 (simjang), and for the heart shape it is 하트 (hateu).

faq.q: What is a finger heart called in Korean?
faq.a: It is called 손하트 (sonhateu), which means "hand heart."

intro: "Star" in Korean is 별 (byeol). It is the native Korean word for the stars in the sky. For a famous person, Koreans usually use the loanword 스타 (seuta).

ways.note: A star in the sky. Short, pretty and very common in songs and names.
A star as in a celebrity, from English "star."
Starlight. A soft, poetic word.
A constellation, and also a star sign in astrology.
The morning star (Venus). Also used for a rising new talent.

examples.context: Lying outside at night
Camping in the countryside
examples.en: There are so many stars in the sky.

examples.context: A note to someone special

tips: 별 is one of the most popular Korean tattoo and caption words. It is a complete word on its own, and it also appears in given names such as 한별 (hanbyeol).
The ㄹ at the end of byeol is a light l sound. Say it like "byul" with a short vowel.
Use 별 for stars in the sky and 스타 for celebrities. Calling a singer 별 sounds poetic rather than everyday.

faq.q: How do you say star in Korean?
faq.a: Star is 별 (byeol). For a celebrity, Koreans say 스타 (seuta).

faq.q: How do you say starlight in Korean?
faq.a: Starlight is 별빛 (byeolbit).

intro: "Moon" in Korean is 달 (dal). It is a short native Korean word and is used for the moon in every situation. A full moon is 보름달 (boreumdal).

ways.note: The moon. Also means "month," so context tells you which one.
A full moon. Closely tied to Chuseok and the first full moon of the lunar year.
A half moon.
A thin crescent moon, seen early in the lunar month.
Moonlight. A soft, poetic word.

examples.context: Walking home at night
Looking out the window
Asking a friend to go outside

tips: 달 also means "month." 한 달 (han dal) is "one month," so do not be surprised to see it in calendar talk.
Do not mix up 달 (dal, moon) with 딸 (ttal, daughter). The ㄸ in 딸 is a tense, stronger sound.
On Chuseok night, many Koreans look at the full moon and make a wish. 달 and 달빛 are popular for captions and tattoos.

faq.q: How do you say full moon in Korean?
faq.a: A full moon is 보름달 (boreumdal).

faq.q: Does 달 mean moon or month?
faq.a: Both. 달 means moon, and it also means month, as in 한 달 (one month).

intro: "Sun" in Korean is 해 (hae). This is the everyday word. The Sino-Korean word 태양 (taeyang) also means sun and sounds a bit grander, so you see it in science, songs and names.

ways.note: The everyday native word for the sun, as in sunrise or sunset.
The sun as a celestial body. Used in science and in poetic or powerful language.
Sunlight.
Rays of sunshine. A warm, gentle word that is popular in captions.
Sunrise. Many Koreans go to see the first sunrise of the new year.

examples.context: Waking up early on a trip
Sitting in a café by the window
A sweet message to a partner

tips: 해 has other meanings too. It can mean "year" (새해, new year), and 해 is also a casual form of the verb "do." Context makes it clear.
In everyday speech, Koreans say 해 for the sun. 태양 sounds more formal or dramatic, which is why it suits song lyrics and stage names.
For a caption or tattoo, 햇살 (sunshine) is a gentle, positive choice.

faq.q: What is the difference between 해 and 태양?
faq.a: Both mean sun. 해 is the everyday native word, and 태양 is the Sino-Korean word used in science and more poetic language.

faq.q: How do you say sunshine in Korean?
faq.a: Sunshine is 햇살 (haetsal), and sunlight is 햇빛 (haetbit).

intro: "Sky" in Korean is 하늘 (haneul). It is the native Korean word for the sky and is used in every situation. The night sky is 밤하늘 (bamhaneul).

ways.note: The sky. Also used for heaven in some expressions.
The night sky.
A blue sky. A common, slightly poetic phrase.
Sky blue, the color. Literally "sky color."

examples.context: Opening the curtains in the morning
Stargazing with a friend
examples.en: The night sky is so pretty.

examples.context: Pointing out a sunset

tips: 하늘 is also used as a given name for both girls and boys, so it is a well-loved word for names and tattoos.
The vowel in 늘 is 으 (eu), a short sound made with flat lips. Say it like "ha-nool" but with your lips unrounded.
Some expressions use 하늘 to mean heaven or fate, such as 하늘이 도왔다, "heaven helped."

faq.q: How do you say sky in Korean?
faq.a: Sky is 하늘 (haneul).

faq.q: Is Haneul a Korean name?
faq.a: Yes. 하늘 is used as a given name for both girls and boys.

intro: "Flower" in Korean is 꽃 (kkot). It is the native Korean word for any flower. Its sound changes a little before a vowel, so 꽃이 is pronounced kkochi.

ways.note: Flower. The everyday word for any kind of flower.
A petal. Pronounced kkon-nip because of sound changes.
A bouquet.
Literally "flower road." Used to wish someone a happy, easy future.
"Flower boy," a very good-looking young man. Often spelled kkotminam by fans.

examples.context: Walking through a park in spring
Coming home from the market
Cheering on a friend or an idol
examples.en: Let's walk only on flower roads.

tips: The final ㅊ in 꽃 is said like a t when the word stands alone (kkot). Before a vowel it becomes ch: 꽃이 (kkochi), 꽃을 (kkocheul).
Fans often tell idols 꽃길만 걷자, "let's walk only on flower roads," which means "I wish you only good things ahead."
꽃 works well alone for a tattoo or caption. The doubled ㄲ is a tense k sound, stronger than a normal k.

faq.q: How do you say flower in Korean?
faq.a: Flower is 꽃 (kkot).

faq.q: What does kkotgil mean?
faq.a: 꽃길 means "flower road." Wishing someone 꽃길 means wishing them a happy, easy path in life.

intro: "Cherry blossom" in Korean is 벚꽃 (beotkkot). It joins 벚 (cherry tree) and 꽃 (flower). In spring, Koreans go out in crowds to see them.

ways.note: Cherry blossom. The standard word, used everywhere.
A cherry tree. Pronounced beon-namu.
Going out to enjoy spring flowers, often cherry blossoms.
A cherry blossom festival.

examples.context: Noticing the trees on the way to work
Making weekend plans in April
examples.en: Let's go see the cherry blossoms.

examples.context: Posting a spring photo
examples.en: The cherry blossoms are so pretty.

tips: Cherry blossom season in Korea is usually from late March to mid April. Jinhae and Yeouido in Seoul are well known places to see them.
Koreans say 벚꽃, not the Japanese word sakura.
The ㅊ at the end of 벚 sounds like a t, and the ㄲ in 꽃 is a tense k: beot-kkot. 벚꽃 is a lovely spring caption word.

faq.q: How do you say cherry blossom in Korean?
faq.a: Cherry blossom is 벚꽃 (beotkkot).

faq.q: When do cherry blossoms bloom in Korea?
faq.a: Usually from late March to mid April, starting in the south and moving north.

intro: "Butterfly" in Korean is 나비 (nabi). It is a short native Korean word, easy to say and easy to write. 나비 is also a classic name for cats in Korea.

ways.note: Butterfly. The everyday word.
A swallowtail butterfly. Literally "tiger butterfly."
A white butterfly.
A moth. Good to know so you do not mix the two up.
A bow tie. Literally "butterfly necktie."

examples.context: Watching a garden in summer
Introducing your pet
Showing a friend new ink

tips: 나비 is one of the most traditional names for a cat in Korea, a bit like "Kitty" in English.
The butterfly effect is 나비 효과 (nabi hyogwa).
나비 is a popular tattoo and caption word. It is a complete word on its own and looks simple and neat in Hangul.

faq.q: How do you say butterfly in Korean?
faq.a: Butterfly is 나비 (nabi).

faq.q: Why are Korean cats called Nabi?
faq.a: 나비 has long been a traditional cat name in Korea, much like "Kitty" in English.

intro: "Rain" in Korean is 비 (bi). To say it is raining, Koreans say the rain "comes": 비가 와 (biga wa).

ways.note: Rain. The everyday word.
A sudden, short shower, typical of summer.
The rainy season in early summer, usually late June to July.
A light drizzle.
The sound of rain.

examples.context: Looking out the window
Checking the weather app
examples.en: They say it's going to rain.

examples.context: Relaxing indoors on a rainy day
examples.en: The sound of rain is so nice.

tips: Korean does not have a verb like "to rain." You say rain comes (비가 오다) and rain stops (비가 그치다).
On rainy days, many Koreans crave 파전 (pajeon, savory pancake) with 막걸리 (makgeolli, rice wine).
The singer Rain's Korean stage name is simply 비. 비 is a single short syllable with other meanings too, so for a tattoo or caption, 빗소리 (sound of rain) or 소나기 may feel more complete.

faq.q: How do you say it's raining in Korean?
faq.a: Say 비가 와 (biga wa) casually, or 비가 와요 (biga wayo) politely.

faq.q: What is jangma?
faq.a: 장마 (jangma) is Korea's rainy season, usually from late June through July.

intro: "Snow" in Korean is 눈 (nun). Like rain, snow "comes" in Korean, so "it's snowing" is 눈이 와 (nuni wa). Note that 눈 also means "eye."

ways.note: Snow. Same spelling as the word for eye.
The first snow of the year. A romantic idea in Korea.
Big, fluffy snowflakes falling heavily.
A snowflake.
A snowman. Literally "snow person."

examples.context: Waking up to a white street
Texting someone on a winter night
Playing outside with kids

tips: 눈 means both "snow" and "eye." Context almost always makes it clear: 눈이 와 is "it's snowing," while 눈이 예뻐 is "your eyes are pretty."

첫눈 (first snow) is special in Korea. Many people text friends or partners when it falls, and there is a folk belief that if your nail dye from summer balsam flowers lasts until the first snow, your love will come true.
첫눈 is pronounced cheon-nun because of a sound change.

faq.q: How do you say it's snowing in Korean?
faq.a: Say 눈이 와 (nuni wa) casually, or 눈이 와요 (nuni wayo) politely.

faq.q: Why does 눈 mean both snow and eye?
faq.a: They are two different words that happen to be spelled the same. Context tells you which one is meant.

intro: "Sea" in Korean is 바다 (bada). It covers both "sea" and "ocean," and it is also what people say when they mean going to the beach.

ways.note: Sea or ocean. The everyday word.
The seaside or the beach.
A beach. A Sino-Korean word, common on signs and in travel writing.
A wave.
Seawater. Pronounced badan-mul.

examples.context: Stuck in the city on a hot day
examples.en: I want to see the sea.

examples.context: Planning a summer trip
Sitting on the sand at night
examples.en: The sound of the waves is so nice.

tips: Koreans usually say 바다 가자, "let's go to the sea," where English speakers might say "let's go to the beach."
Busan's 해운대 (Haeundae) is Korea's most famous beach, and the east coast is known for clear water and sunrise views.
바다 is a calm, open word that works well on its own for captions and tattoos.

faq.q: How do you say ocean in Korean?
faq.a: Koreans use 바다 (bada) for both sea and ocean. Large oceans have names with 양, like 태평양 (Pacific Ocean).

faq.q: How do you say beach in Korean?
faq.a: Beach is 바닷가 (badatga) or 해변 (haebyeon). In speech, people often just say 바다.

intro: "Dream" in Korean is 꿈 (kkum). It means both a dream you have while sleeping and a dream for the future. To dream is 꿈을 꾸다 (kkumeul kkuda).

ways.note: A dream, both while sleeping and as a goal in life.
To dream. A verb, also written 꿈을 꾸다.
A nightmare.
Dreamland. A cute word for falling asleep.
A conception dream, said to foretell a baby's birth.

examples.context: Saying good night
Talking about the future
examples.en: My dream is to be a singer.

examples.context: Telling a friend over breakfast
examples.en: I had a weird dream last night.

tips: In Korean you do not "have" a dream, you 꾸다 it: 꿈을 꾸다. In casual speech the particle often drops: 꿈 꿨어.
Many Koreans take dreams seriously. Dreaming of a pig is thought to bring good luck, and some people buy a lottery ticket after one.
꿈 is a popular tattoo and caption word. The ㄲ is a tense k sound, stronger than a normal k.

faq.q: How do you say dream in Korean?
faq.a: Dream is 꿈 (kkum). It works for both sleeping dreams and life goals.

faq.q: How do you say sweet dreams in Korean?
faq.a: A common way is 좋은 꿈 꿔 (joeun kkum kkwo), "have a good dream." 잘 자 (good night) is also very common.

intro: "Hope" in Korean is 희망 (huimang). It is the noun for hope, as in "don't lose hope." To say "I hope," Koreans use the verb 바라다 (barada).

ways.note: Hope as a noun. Common in speeches, songs and captions.
To hope or wish. Used for "I hope that..."
A deep, heartfelt wish. Feels a little more personal than 희망.
A wish. The same spelling also means wind.
Expectation, looking forward to something.

examples.context: Comforting a friend
Hearing that a patient is improving
Writing a card for a friend

tips: 희망 is pronounced "hee-mang." The 의 in 희 sounds like 이 because it follows a consonant.
For "I hope," the correct form is 바라 or 바라요. Many people write 바래, which is common but not standard spelling.
희망 is a good tattoo or caption word on its own. 소망 is softer and more personal, closer to "a heartfelt wish."

faq.q: How do you say hope in Korean?
faq.a: Hope is 희망 (huimang). To say "I hope," use 바라다 (barada), as in 바라요 (barayo).

faq.q: Is it 바라 or 바래?
faq.a: The standard form is 바라 (bara). 바래 is very common in speech and texts but is not standard spelling.

intro: "Life" in Korean is most often 인생 (insaeng), meaning one's life as a whole journey. The native word 삶 (sam) is more poetic, and 생명 (saengmyeong) means life as in being alive.

ways.note: Life as a whole, one's journey through life. The most common word in speech.
Life and living. A native word that feels thoughtful and poetic.
Life as in being alive, the life of a living thing.
Daily life or lifestyle, as in school life or married life.
One's life, the breath of life. Used for risking or saving a life.

examples.context: Deciding to take a trip
Relaxing with good food
Checking photos after a trip
examples.en: I got the best photo of my life.

tips: Korean has several words for life. Use 인생 for your life story, 삶 for life in a deeper sense, 생명 for being alive, and 생활 for daily routine.
In slang, 인생 before a noun means "the best of my life": 인생 사진 (best photo ever), 인생 맛집 (best restaurant ever), 인생 드라마 (favorite drama ever).
삶 is a beautiful tattoo word. It is pronounced "sam" because the ㄹ is silent here.

faq.q: What is the Korean word for life?
faq.a: The most common is 인생 (insaeng). 삶 (sam) is more poetic, and 생명 (saengmyeong) means being alive.

faq.q: What does insaeng shot mean?
faq.a: 인생 사진 or 인생샷 is slang for the best photo of your life, one where you look amazing.

intro: "Forever" in Korean is 영원히 (yeongwonhi). It is an adverb, so it usually goes right before a verb, as in 영원히 사랑해 (I will love you forever). The noun "eternity" is 영원 (yeongwon).

ways.note: The everyday word for "forever." Use it before a verb: 영원히 함께해 (be with me forever).
The noun: "eternity" or "forever" as a thing. Common in titles and short phrases like 영원한 사랑.
"Eternal," used before a noun: 영원한 사랑 (eternal love), 영원한 친구 (friends forever).
"For life" or "all my life." Very natural in real promises: 평생 함께하자 (let's be together for life).
"Always, for as long as it lasts." A soft, slightly poetic word often found in letters and songs.

examples.context: Writing in an anniversary card
Hugging your best friend at graduation
A quiet promise to a partner

tips: 영원히 is one of the most popular words for tattoos and couple rings, and it looks good on its own. If you want a noun rather than an adverb, 영원 (eternity) or 영원한 사랑 (eternal love) also work well.

In real conversation, Koreans often say 평생 (for life) instead of 영원히 when making a promise, because it sounds more down to earth. 영원히 can feel a little dramatic, which is exactly why it is common in song lyrics and love letters.
Pronunciation: the ㅎ in 영원히 is very soft, so it often sounds like "yeong-won-i."

faq.q: How do you say "I love you forever" in Korean?
faq.a: 영원히 사랑해 (yeongwonhi saranghae) is the casual way, for a partner or close friend. The polite version is 영원히 사랑해요 (yeongwonhi saranghaeyo).

faq.q: What is the difference between 영원히 and 영원?
faq.a: 영원히 is an adverb ("forever," describing how you do something), while 영원 is a noun ("eternity"). Say 영원히 사랑해, but 영원한 사랑 for "eternal love."

faq.q: How do you say "forever and always" in Korean?
faq.a: There is no single fixed phrase, but 언제까지나 영원히 (eonjekkajina yeongwonhi) carries that feeling of "always and forever."

intro: "Peace" in Korean is 평화 (pyeonghwa). It is used for world peace as well as for a calm, peaceful feeling. To describe something as peaceful, use 평화로운 (pyeonghwaroun).

ways.note: The standard word for "peace," from world peace to a peaceful afternoon.
"Peaceful," used before a noun: 평화로운 아침 (a peaceful morning).
"Inner peace," literally "peace of the heart."
"Calm" or "tranquility." A quieter, more personal kind of peace, often in 평온한 하루 (a calm day).
"Peace and well-being." Common in blessings and religious greetings, such as 평안하세요 (may you be at peace).

examples.context: Talking about a charity event
Sitting by a lake on vacation
Telling a friend how you feel after yoga

tips: 평화 is a lovely word for a tattoo or name and reads fine on its own. It comes from the Chinese characters 平和, meaning "even" and "harmony."
The peace sign you make with two fingers in photos is called 브이 (beui), from the letter V. Koreans almost never call it a "peace sign."
평화 sounds a bit big and serious in casual chat. To say a place or a day felt peaceful, Koreans usually use 평화롭다 or 여유롭다 (relaxed and unhurried).

faq.q: What do Koreans call the peace sign in photos?
faq.a: They call it 브이 (beui), after the letter V. A photographer might say 브이 해 봐 (do a V) before taking the picture.

faq.q: How do you say "inner peace" in Korean?
faq.a: 마음의 평화 (maeumui pyeonghwa), literally "peace of the heart."

faq.q: How do you say "peaceful" in Korean?
faq.a: Use 평화로운 (pyeonghwaroun) before a noun, like 평화로운 밤 (a peaceful night), or 평화로워요 (pyeonghwarowoyo) to say "it's peaceful."

intro: "Angel" in Korean is 천사 (cheonsa). Koreans use it both for real angels and for very kind or sweet people, especially babies. To say someone is angelic, say 천사 같아 (cheonsa gata), "like an angel."

ways.note: The standard word for "angel," also used for a very kind person.
"You're like an angel" or "so angelic." The polite form is 천사 같아요.
"Guardian angel." Also used for someone who always looks out for you.
The English loanword. You see it in brand and shop names more than in conversation.

examples.context: A message to someone special
Looking at a sleeping baby
examples.en: The baby looks like an angel.

examples.context: A friend helps you move house

tips: Koreans sometimes write the number 1004 to mean "angel," because 1004 is read 천사 (cheon-sa: 천 = thousand, 사 = four). You will see it in phone numbers, usernames and cute messages.
천사가 따로 없네 (literally "there is no other angel") is a common way to say "you're an absolute angel" when someone does something kind.
천사 works well alone as a tattoo or nickname. Parents and grandparents often call a baby 우리 천사 (our little angel).

faq.q: Why do Koreans write 1004 for angel?
faq.a: Because the number 1004 is pronounced 천사 (cheon-sa) in Korean, which sounds exactly like the word for angel.

faq.q: How do you say "you are my angel" in Korean?
faq.a: 너는 내 천사야 (neoneun nae cheonsaya) is the casual way. Politely, say 당신은 제 천사예요, though most people only say this casually to someone close.

intro: "Princess" in Korean is 공주 (gongju). It means a real princess, and it is also an affectionate name parents use for a little girl. Adding 님 gives 공주님 (gongjunim), which sounds sweeter and more respectful.

ways.note: The standard word for "princess."
"Princess" with the honorific 님. Common when talking sweetly to or about a little girl, and in fairy tales.
"My little princess," literally "our princess." What a doting parent calls a daughter.
"Princess syndrome": a teasing word for a girl who acts like everyone should treat her like royalty.
A historical title in Joseon-era dramas: a king's daughter by a concubine, while 공주 is the queen's daughter.

examples.context: A dad waking up his daughter
Complimenting a little girl's dress
examples.en: You're as pretty as a princess.

examples.context: Teasing a friend who wants to be pampered
examples.en: Do you think you're a princess?

tips: When a baby girl is born, people often say 공주님이에요 (it's a princess!). For a baby boy, the matching word is 왕자님 (wangjanim, prince).
In historical K-dramas you will hear both 공주 and 옹주. 공주 is the daughter of the king and queen, while 옹주 is the king's daughter by a concubine.
공주 works on its own as a nickname or caption. Just know that 공주병 is teasing, so calling a grown woman 공주 can sound playful or a little sarcastic depending on tone.

faq.q: What is 공주병?
faq.a: 공주병 (gongjubyeong) means "princess syndrome," a joking term for someone who acts as if she is a princess. It is teasing, not a compliment.

faq.q: How do you say "prince" in Korean?
faq.a: Prince is 왕자 (wangja), or 왕자님 (wangjanim) with the honorific.

faq.q: What is the difference between 공주 and 옹주?
faq.a: Both are a king's daughter. 공주 is born to the queen, and 옹주 is born to a royal concubine. You mostly hear 옹주 in historical dramas.

intro: "King" in Korean is 왕 (wang). It is the everyday word for a king, from fairy tales to history books. In historical K-dramas, people speaking to the king call him 전하 (jeonha), "Your Majesty."

ways.note: The standard word for "king."
The native Korean word for king. It sounds old and is mostly used for kings of the past.
"The monarch of a country." A formal word used in news, such as for a king who reigns today.
"Your Majesty." How courtiers address the king in Joseon-era dramas.
The English loanword, used in games, chess and cards, and in slang like 킹받네 ("so annoying").

examples.context: Reading a fairy tale to a child
Watching a nature documentary
examples.en: The lion is the king of animals.

examples.context: A child playing pretend

tips: In historical dramas, the king is called 전하 (jeonha) to his face, and an emperor is called 폐하 (pyeha). The king refers to himself with the special word 과인 (gwain).
왕 also works as a prefix meaning "big": 왕만두 (giant dumpling), 왕눈이 (someone with big eyes). In playful speech it can mean "super," as in 왕 짜증 (super annoying).
王, the Chinese character for king, is well known in Korea. For a tattoo or caption, 왕 alone is fine, though it reads as a plain word, not a title.

faq.q: How do you say "Your Majesty" in Korean?
faq.a: In historical dramas, a king is addressed as 전하 (jeonha), and an emperor as 폐하 (pyeha).

faq.q: What does 킹받네 mean?
faq.a: It is slang for "so annoying," a pun on 열받네 (it makes me mad), with 킹 (king) making it stronger. Use it only with friends.

intro: "Queen" in Korean is 여왕 (yeowang), a woman who rules a country. A king's wife is a different word, 왕비 (wangbi). In everyday slang, Koreans also say 퀸 (kwin) for a woman they admire.

ways.note: A ruling queen, literally "female king." Also used for "queen" in titles, like 눈의 여왕 (The Snow Queen).
Queen consort: the king's wife. This is the queen you meet in most historical dramas.
A formal title for a queen consort, used in official names and history.
How the queen consort is referred to in Joseon-era dramas. Servants say 중전마마 (jungjeonmama).
The English loanword. Used for chess and playing cards, and as praise for an admired woman.

examples.context: Hyping up a friend before a big night
Reading a fairy tale to a child
examples.en: There lived a king and a queen.

examples.context: Bragging about your older sister (said by a girl)
examples.en: My sister is a total queen.

tips: The biggest mistake learners make is mixing up 여왕 and 왕비. 여왕 rules on her own. 왕비 is married to the king. Korea's Silla kingdom had real ruling queens, such as Queen Seondeok (선덕여왕).
In historical K-dramas, the queen consort is usually called 중전 (jungjeon) by the king and 중전마마 (jungjeonmama) by servants.
For a caption or tattoo, 여왕 reads clearly on its own. 퀸 feels more like slang or fan talk.

faq.q: What is the difference between 여왕 and 왕비?
faq.a: 여왕 (yeowang) is a queen who rules. 왕비 (wangbi) is the wife of a king.

faq.q: What do they call the queen in K-dramas?
faq.a: In Joseon-era dramas she is called 중전 (jungjeon), and palace servants address her as 중전마마 (jungjeonmama).

intro: "Tiger" in Korean is 호랑이 (horangi). The tiger is one of Korea's best-loved national symbols and appears in many folk tales. An older native word for tiger is 범 (beom).

ways.note: The standard word for "tiger."
An older native word for tiger. Still used in sayings and in 범띠 (Year of the Tiger).
"White tiger," a sacred guardian animal in East Asian tradition.
"Year of the Tiger" in the Korean zodiac. 범띠 (beomtti) means the same.
The sound a tiger makes in Korean: "roar!" Popular when playing with children.

examples.context: At the zoo with a friend
Talking about the zodiac
examples.en: I was born in the Year of the Tiger.

examples.context: Playing with a toddler

tips: Korean folk tales often begin with 호랑이 담배 피우던 시절, "back when tigers smoked," the Korean way of saying "once upon a time."
호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다 ("even the tiger comes when you talk about it") is the Korean version of "speak of the devil."
The tiger was the mascot of two Olympics in Korea: Hodori (호돌이) in 1988 and the white tiger Soohorang (수호랑) in 2018. 호랑이 works well on its own as a tattoo or nickname.

faq.q: How do you say "speak of the devil" in Korean?
faq.a: 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다 (horangido je mal hamyeon onda), "even the tiger comes when you talk about it."

faq.q: What sound does a tiger make in Korean?
faq.a: 어흥 (eoheung). It is the Korean "roar."

faq.q: How do you say Year of the Tiger in Korean?
faq.a: 호랑이띠 (horangitti) or 범띠 (beomtti). 저는 호랑이띠예요 means "I was born in the Year of the Tiger."

intro: "Cat" in Korean is 고양이 (goyangi). Cat lovers often shorten it to the cute 냥이 (nyangi), "kitty." A cat's meow is 야옹 (yaong).

ways.note: The standard word for "cat."
A cute, casual word for a cat, like "kitty." Very common online.
"Kitty cat," made from the meow sound. Used with children or in a playful way.
"Kitten," literally "baby cat."
"Meow," the sound a cat makes in Korean.

examples.context: Asking a new coworker about pets
Showing a friend a photo
Whispering so you don't wake the cat

tips: Korean cat owners jokingly call themselves 집사 (jipsa), "butler," because the cat is clearly the boss of the house.
냥 (nyang) shows up all over Korean cat slang, like 냥스타그램 for cat photos, and some people add 냥 to the end of sentences to sound cute and cat-like.
고양이 is a sweet word for a tattoo, and 냥이 is a popular nickname. A 고양이상 (goyangisang, "cat face") is a person with sharp, upturned eyes.

faq.q: How do cats meow in Korean?
faq.a: Korean cats say 야옹 (yaong).

faq.q: How do you say kitten in Korean?
faq.a: 아기 고양이 (agi goyangi), literally "baby cat." You may also hear 새끼 고양이 (saekki goyangi), but 새끼 is also used as an insult, so 아기 고양이 sounds softer.

faq.q: What does 집사 mean for cat owners?
faq.a: 집사 (jipsa) means "butler." Cat owners use it jokingly about themselves because they serve their cats.

intro: "Dog" in Korean is 개 (gae), but most people call a pet dog 강아지 (gangaji), which literally means "puppy." 강아지 sounds warmer and is the word you will hear most for someone's pet.

ways.note: "Puppy," but used for pet dogs of any age. The friendliest everyday choice.
The basic word for "dog." Neutral in facts and signs, but also used in insults, so it can sound blunt about a pet.
"Doggy," made from the bark sound 멍멍. Used with children or playfully.
Internet slang for "doggo." It comes from 멍멍이, because 댕 and 멍 look alike in writing.
"Companion dog." A formal word used on signs, in news and at the vet.

examples.context: Asking your partner on a sunny day
examples.en: Let's take the dog for a walk.

examples.context: Telling a coworker about your pets
Posting a pet photo

tips: Be careful with 개. As a word for the animal it is fine, but it is also part of many strong insults and slang words, so people usually say 강아지 about their own pet.
Grandparents often call a grandchild 우리 강아지 ("my puppy") as a term of affection. It is a loving thing to say, not an insult.
Korean dogs bark 멍멍 (meongmeong). As a tattoo or nickname, 강아지 or 멍멍이 is cute, while 개 alone may look harsh.

faq.q: How do dogs bark in Korean?
faq.a: Korean dogs say 멍멍 (meongmeong).

faq.q: Is it rude to say 개?
faq.a: Not when you simply mean the animal, but 개 is also used in insults, so 강아지 sounds kinder when you talk about someone's pet.

faq.q: What does 댕댕이 mean?
faq.a: 댕댕이 (daengdaengi) is cute internet slang for a dog, like "doggo." It is a playful spelling of 멍멍이.

intro: "Bunny" in Korean is 토끼 (tokki). The same word covers both "bunny" and "rabbit." For a baby bunny, say 아기 토끼 (agi tokki).

ways.note: The standard word for "rabbit" or "bunny."
"Baby bunny," a cute way to say a young rabbit.
"Mountain rabbit" or wild hare. Also the name of a famous Korean children's song.
"House rabbit," a pet rabbit.
"Year of the Rabbit" in the Korean zodiac.

examples.context: Watching a pet rabbit eat
examples.en: The bunny is eating a carrot.

examples.context: Complimenting a friend's smile
Singing with a child
examples.en: Do you know the Mountain Rabbit song?

tips: In K-pop fan talk, 토끼상 (tokkisang, "bunny face") describes someone with round eyes and a cute, bunny-like smile. It is a compliment.
When Koreans look at the full moon, they traditionally see a rabbit pounding rice cakes, not a man in the moon.
토끼 is a popular nickname and works nicely as a tattoo. It is also a common cute nickname for a girlfriend or a little child.

faq.q: What is 토끼상?
faq.a: 토끼상 (tokkisang) means "bunny face," a face type with round, bright eyes and a cute look. It is often used about K-pop idols.

faq.q: Is there a difference between bunny and rabbit in Korean?
faq.a: Not really. 토끼 means both. To make it sound extra cute, say 아기 토끼 (baby bunny).

intro: "Bear" in Korean is 곰 (gom). A cute or teddy bear is often called 곰돌이 (gomdori), and a stuffed teddy bear is 곰 인형 (gom inhyeong).

ways.note: The standard word for "bear."
A cute word for a bear, like "teddy." Also a sweet nickname for a big, gentle person.
"Teddy bear," literally "bear doll."
"Polar bear."
The Asiatic black bear, named for the half-moon mark on its chest. A protected animal in Korea.

examples.context: Shopping for a birthday present
Telling a friend about a hiking trip
examples.en: I saw a bear in the mountains.

examples.context: A child looking for a toy

tips: In the Korean founding myth, a bear patiently stayed in a cave eating garlic and mugwort and became a woman, who gave birth to Dangun, the legendary founder of Korea. That is why the bear is a symbol of patience in Korea.
Calling someone 곰 같다 ("like a bear") means they are slow, a bit clumsy or not very good at flirting, but usually honest. It is often contrasted with 여우 (fox), someone clever and charming.
곰 is a short, sweet word for a tattoo or nickname, and 곰돌이 is a favorite nickname between couples. 곰 세 마리 ("Three Bears") is a children's song almost every Korean knows.

faq.q: How do you say teddy bear in Korean?
faq.a: 곰 인형 (gom inhyeong), literally "bear doll." Kids also just say 곰돌이 (gomdori).

faq.q: What does it mean to call someone a bear in Korean?
faq.a: 곰 같다 means someone is slow or not very smooth or flirty, but often in a kind, honest way. It is teasing rather than a harsh insult.

intro: "Dragon" in Korean is 용 (yong). This is the East Asian dragon: wise, lucky and linked to water and the sky. For the fire-breathing dragon of Western fantasy and games, Koreans often say 드래곤 (deuraegon).

ways.note: The standard word for "dragon," usually the lucky East Asian kind.
The English loanword, used for Western fantasy dragons in games, movies and books.
An old native Korean word for dragon. Rare in speech, but used in names and brands.
"Blue dragon," the guardian of the east in East Asian tradition.
"Year of the Dragon" in the Korean zodiac.

examples.context: Admiring art at a temple
Talking about the zodiac
examples.en: I was born in the Year of the Dragon.

examples.context: Talking about someone from humble beginnings
examples.en: A dragon rises from a small stream.

tips: In Korean culture, dragons are lucky, not scary. Dreaming of a dragon, a 용꿈 (yongkkum), is one of the best dreams you can have, and it is a classic 태몽 (taemong), a dream that announces a pregnancy.
The proverb 개천에서 용 난다 ("a dragon rises from a small stream") describes someone who achieves great success despite a humble background.
The Chinese character 龍 is read 용 at the start of a word but 룡 after another syllable, so "blue dragon" is 청룡. Fun fact: "dinosaur" is 공룡 (gongnyong), literally "terrifying dragon."

faq.q: Is 공룡 a dragon?
faq.a: No, 공룡 (gongnyong) means dinosaur, even though its second syllable is the same character as dragon.

faq.q: What is a dragon dream in Korea?
faq.a: A 용꿈 (yongkkum) is a dream about a dragon. It is considered very lucky and is often seen as a sign of great success or of a coming baby.

intro: "Beautiful" in Korean is 아름다운 (areumdaun) when it comes before a noun, as in 아름다운 밤 (a beautiful night). To say "it's beautiful," use 아름다워요 (areumdawoyo). For people, Koreans more often say 예뻐 (yeppeo), "pretty."

ways.note: "Beautiful" before a noun: 아름다운 노래 (a beautiful song), 아름다운 사람 (a beautiful person).
"It's beautiful." Good for scenery, music or art.
"It's beautiful," casual. For friends, family and partners.
The dictionary form. Also used as an exclamation to yourself, or in writing.
"Pretty." The everyday way to compliment how someone or something looks.
"Pretty," polite. Fine for strangers and coworkers.

examples.context: Watching a sunset with a tour guide
Looking up at the stars
Complimenting your girlfriend

tips: 아름답다 sounds deep and a little formal, so it suits nature, music, art and heartfelt moments. For everyday compliments on looks, 예쁘다 is far more common. For men, people usually say 잘생겼다 (handsome) or 멋있다 (cool).
The ㅂ at the end of 아름답 changes to 워 when you add an ending: 아름답다 becomes 아름다워요. This is a common pattern, so it is worth remembering.
아름다운 alone feels unfinished, like "beautiful..." without a noun. For a tattoo or caption, a short phrase such as 아름다운 날 (a beautiful day) reads more naturally.

faq.q: What is the difference between 아름답다 and 예쁘다?
faq.a: 예쁘다 means "pretty" and is the everyday compliment. 아름답다 means "beautiful" and is deeper and more poetic, often used for scenery, music or a beautiful heart.

faq.q: How do you say "you are beautiful" in Korean?
faq.a: Most Koreans say 예뻐 (yeppeo) casually or 예뻐요 (yeppeoyo) politely. 아름다워요 (areumdawoyo) is also correct but sounds more romantic and serious.

intro: "Strong" in Korean is 강한 (ganghan) when it comes before a noun, as in 강한 사람 (a strong person). To say "you are strong," use 강해 (ganghae) casually or 강해요 (ganghaeyo) politely. For physical strength, Koreans say 힘이 세다 (himi seda).

ways.note: "Strong" before a noun: 강한 사람 (a strong person), 강한 마음 (a strong heart).
"You're strong" or "it's strong," casual.
"Strong," polite.
"Physically strong," literally "strength is strong." Used for muscles and lifting things.
"Sturdy" or "healthy and strong." Used for bodies, children and well-built things.
"Tough, resilient." Describes a strong will or character, a bit formal.

examples.context: Comforting a friend after a hard year
A child bragging about their dad
Cheering a friend up before an exam

tips: To tell someone to "stay strong," Koreans almost always say 힘내 (himnae) or 힘내요 (himnaeyo), which literally means "bring out your strength."
세다 is also "strong" in everyday speech, for wind, alcohol and personalities. A 센 언니 is a confident, tough woman, and 술이 세다 means someone can hold their drink.
강한 alone sounds unfinished as a tattoo, like an adjective waiting for a noun. Nouns such as 힘 (him, strength) or 용기 (yonggi, courage) read better on their own.

faq.q: How do you say "stay strong" in Korean?
faq.a: Koreans say 힘내 (himnae) casually or 힘내세요 (himnaeseyo) politely. It means "cheer up" or "stay strong."

faq.q: What is the difference between 강하다 and 세다?
faq.a: Both mean strong. 강하다 is general and also works for emotional strength. 세다 is more conversational and is used for physical power, wind, drinks and strong personalities.

intro: "Happiness" in Korean is 행복 (haengbok). To say "I'm happy," add 해: 행복해 (haengbokhae), or politely 행복해요 (haengbokhaeyo). 행복 is a warm, common word in cards, captions and wishes.

ways.note: The noun "happiness."
"I'm happy," casual. A deep, content kind of happy.
"I'm happy," polite.
"Happy" before a noun: 행복한 하루 (a happy day).
"Joy." Closer to the excited happiness of good news.

examples.context: Writing in a birthday card
A quiet moment with a partner
examples.en: I'm happy when I'm with you.

examples.context: A caption under a family photo

tips: 행복하세요 ("be happy") is a very common blessing in cards and goodbyes, and 행복한 하루 보내세요 means "have a happy day."
행복 describes a deep, lasting happiness, while 기쁘다 is the joy you feel at good news. When something small makes you happy, Koreans also say 좋아 (I like it) or 신나 (I'm excited).
행복 is one of the most popular Korean words for tattoos and looks good on its own. In fast speech the ㅎ in 행복해 is soft, so it can sound like "haeng-bo-kae."

faq.q: How do you say "I'm happy" in Korean?
faq.a: 행복해 (haengbokhae) casually or 행복해요 (haengbokhaeyo) politely. For quick joy at good news, 기뻐 (gippeo) also works.

faq.q: How do you say "be happy" in Korean?
faq.a: 행복하세요 (haengbokhaseyo) is the polite, warm way, common in cards. To a close friend, 행복해 (haengbokhae) or 행복하자 (let's be happy) works.
